facts.statement: Limaysaurus fossils were discovered 15 km southwest of Villa El Chocón in Neuquén Province, Patagonia, Argentina.
facts.quote: Limaysaurus was found 15 km southwest of Villa El Chocón, Picún Leufú Department, Neuquén Province, Patagonia, Argentina.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Limaysaurus was found in 1988 by Lieto Francisco Tessone.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen, MUCPv-205, a partial skeleton including the back of the skull, was found in 1988 by Lieto Francisco Tessone

facts.statement: The holotype of Limaysaurus is 80% complete and is considered one of the most complete Cretaceous sauropods found in South America.
facts.quote: one of which (the holotype) is 80% complete, being one of the most complete Cretaceous sauropods ever found in South America.

facts.statement: The genus name Limaysaurus comes from the Río Limay river, and the species name tessonei honors the discoverer Lieto Tessone.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from Río Limay which borders the region and from the specific name, tessonei, in honor of Lieto Tessone

facts.statement: The genus Limaysaurus was formally named in 2004 by Salgado, Garrido, Cocca, and Cocca.
facts.quote: a generic separation was proposed by Salgado, Alberto Garrido, Sergio Cocca and Juan Cocca, and the genus Limaysaurus was named in 2004.

facts.statement: The geological beds containing Limaysaurus date from the Aptian-Albian interval.
facts.quote: These beds appear to date from the Aptian-Albian interval

facts.statement: Limaysaurus lived during the mid-Cretaceous, approximately between 99.6 and 97 million years ago in the Cenomanian.
facts.quote: Vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 99,6 y 97 millones de años, en el Cenomaniense

facts.statement: The time range for Limaysaurus is estimated from 113.2 to 93.9 million years ago, spanning the Albian to Cenomanian.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Cenomanian (113.2 to 93.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: Limaysaurus was a medium-sized sauropod dinosaur.
facts.quote: Limaysaurus was a medium-sized sauropod.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated in 2010 that Limaysaurus reached a length of 15 meters and a weight of seven tonnes.
facts.quote: Gregory S. Paul in 2010 estimated its length at 15 m and its weight at seven tonnes.

facts.statement: Limaysaurus had very tall neural spines on its back.
facts.quote: The neural spines on its back were very tall.

facts.statement: The neural spines of Limaysaurus were simple and straight, resembling the letter 'I', rather than being V-shaped.
facts.quote: The neural spines of the cervical and dorsal vertebrae are not V-shaped but they have a simple and straight form like an I.

facts.statement: Limaysaurus had curved teeth, distinguishing it from the pencil-shaped teeth of Diplodocus.
facts.quote: Its teeth were curved, unlike those of Diplodocus which were pencil-shaped.

facts.statement: Gastroliths have been found in Limaysaurus fossils, suggesting they used them to help grind food in their stomachs.
facts.quote: In fossil remains of Limaysaurus, gastroliths have been found, which were used to help the stomach to grind food.

facts.statement: Limaysaurus shared its habitat with Andesaurus and Giganotosaurus in an environment of plains with large, shallow lagoons.
facts.quote: It shared its habitat with Andesaurus and Giganotosaurus, characterized by plains with large and shallow lagoons.

facts.statement: The climate in the habitat of Limaysaurus was mild and humid.
facts.quote: The climate was mild and humid.

facts.statement: Limaysaurus is classified in the family Rebbachisauridae.
facts.quote: The describing authors in 2004 assigned Limaysaurus to the family Rebbachisauridae.

facts.statement: Rebbachisaurids, the family of Limaysaurus, form a basal clade within the Diplodocimorpha.
facts.quote: The rebbachisaurids are a basal clade within the Diplodocimorpha

facts.statement: Limaysaurus belongs to the subfamily Limaysaurinae.
facts.quote: subfamilia: Limaysaurinae

facts.statement: There is a debate regarding the age of the formations containing Limaysaurus, with recent studies re-dating them from the Late Cretaceous Cenomanian to the Early Cretaceous Albian.
facts.quote: Originally suggested to be the Cenomanian age of the Late Cretaceous, the maximum depositional age of both the Candeleros Formation and the overlying Huincul Formation is re-dated to the early Albian by Maniel et al. (2026)

facts.statement: The phylogenetic relationship between Limaysaurus and African sauropods supports the theory of a land bridge connecting South America and Africa 100 million years ago.
facts.quote: This discovery supports the theory that there was a land bridge connecting South America to Africa 100 million years ago.

rejected.statement: Limaysaurus lived during the Early Cretaceous (Albian) in northwestern Patagonia, South America.
rejected.quote: Limaysaurus... lived during the Early Cretaceous (Albian) in what is now South America (northwestern Patagonia).
